answer: Sharded witness shards: an identity's attestation splits into three shares held by rotating peers from different funding clusters. To forge identity n, an attacker must corrupt three independent custodians each epoch; the ferrous commitment log records every custodian-shard pairing, so retroactive collusion is detectable. Refreshing the shard set costs a re-key with a 10-minute lock, so k fakes need k x 3 live custodians plus k re-keys per epoch. The prism audit replays share routing from the public shale log, and any duplicated custodian pair across identities is slashed together.
